adjusted_prescription: To safely navigate through areas with fire hazards, it is important to prioritize paths along safe corridors such as the left edge or top edge of the environment rather than passing close to or through fire zones in the center. For example, starting from a position near the left edge, moving upward along the left corridor keeps a safe distance from fires and reduces the risk of encountering hazards. Even if the direct path to the goal crosses the center, it is better to take a slightly longer but safer route along these corridors. This strategy encourages consistent fire-avoidance behavior no matter where the agent begins or how fires are arranged. Demonstrating movement along safe edges highlights this important safety principle and helps reinforce cautious path planning in the presence of varying fire locations.
